thread:
sasha: Starting bring-up for harbor14b (community fork). Did an int4 canary on a 4xA100 dedicated node. Seeing intermittent OOMs under load and what looks like heap fragmentation rather than a single large alloc failure. Posting the tail of a worker log:
```
  2026-02-18 14:02:11.342 ERROR runtime: allocate failed: requested 2147483648 bytes
  2026-02-18 14:02:11.342 WARN  kvcache: entries=1280 used=68% free_frags=42
  2026-02-18 14:02:11.343 INFO  alloc: small-allocs: 1.2GB, large-allocs: 3.8GB
  ```

tom: Thanks — can you paste the batch / max_new_tokens config you used for the canary?

sasha: Sure, current canary config (pasted from route):
```
  model: harbor14b-int4
  batch_size: 8
  max_new_tokens: 256
  prefetch: true
  kv_evict_threshold: 0.5
  quant_mode: int4
  concurrency_limit: 40
  ```
liam: Looks like classic fragmentation: lots of small allocations after KV cache growth and then a few medium allocations fail. Immediate suggestions: lower `max_new_tokens` default for this model to 128 (reduces worst-case per-request KV growth), drop `batch_size` 8->4 for int4 canary, and flip `prefetch=false` so we don't over-commit memory during async prefetch. Also bump `kv_evict_threshold` to 0.6 so evictions happen earlier.

maya: Quick note on quality — int4 showed a small regress on our eval slice: delta ~ -3% on the hallucination metric and +2.8% perplexity vs fp16 on the small Q&A set. Might be dataset-sensitive; worth running mixed-quant fallback (int4 except attention/first-layer in int8) before we commit defaults.

eval-bot: Eval run 2026-02-18T14:30Z attached: id=eval-20260218-harbor-int4-01. Summary: int4 vs fp16 -> EM -2.9%, PPL +2.7%. Mixed-quant prototype id=eval-20260218-harbor-mixed-01 gave EM -1.1%, PPL +1.1%.

sasha: Plan: roll the int4 canary with these safe defaults: `max_new_tokens=128`, `batch_size=4`, `prefetch=false`, `kv_evict_threshold=0.6`. Monitor OOMs and token-level latency. If OOMs persist we'll deploy a small allocator patch that does periodic compaction and a short-lived KV trim pass after heavy generation sequences. I'll also trigger the mixed-quant test across the canary pool. :hammer_and_wrench:

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled -> pool: harbor-canary-dedicated, start: 2026-02-18T15:10:00Z, strategy: gradual 10% -> 50% over 20m.

dena: If fragmentation proves systemic we should add a soft per-request memory cap + early-NACK policy (return 503 with retry-after) rather than catastrophic OOMs. Also reminder: update model onboarding guide with recommended defaults for int4 (batch=4, max_new_tokens=128, prefetch=false) so solutions-engineering doesn't re-roll risky configs.

sasha: Agree. I'll open a short PR against docs and the model catalog after the canary results. Thanks all.
